title: Local free frames construct a morphism and its twisting-module isomorphism
statement: Let $X,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a coordinate type, and $g:X\to S$. Let $M$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $s_i\in\Gamma(X,M)$, and $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ an open cover of $X$. Suppose that each $s_i|_{U_i}$ is a free generator: for every $V\subseteq U_i$, multiplication by $s_i|_V$ is a bijection $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)\to M(V)$ [def-sc-section-generating-locus]. There is a morphism $\varphi:X\to\mathbb P(I;S)$ over $g$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and an isomorphism $\varphi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong M$ carrying every pulled-back coordinate $T_j$ to $s_j$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback]. No finiteness, nonemptiness, or separate invertibility hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Lemma 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), existence proof, specialized to degree-one polynomial coordinates

proof.text: On U_i write s_j=r_ij s_i. The free-generator hypothesis gives unique coefficients and the cocycle identities. The polynomial affine-chart correspondence constructs the local morphism from the r_ij, with r_ii=1. These local morphisms agree on intersections.

Glue the local morphisms. The free-generator construction in source OfInvertible defines the module morphism locally by sending the pulled-back T_i to s_i; the cocycle identities make these maps agree. Its local inverses glue too, hence it is an isomorphism. The ratio equations show it sends every pulled-back T_j to s_j. These are the source declarations homOfIsFreeGenerator, twistRestrictHom, and exists_hom_twistRestrict.
